descriptions.data: Forge (also called `node-forge`) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to version 1.3.0, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification code is lenient in checking the digest algorithm structure. This can allow a crafted structure that steals padding bytes and uses unchecked portion of the PKCS#1 encoded message to forge a signature when a low public exponent is being used. The issue has been addressed in `node-forge` version 1.3.0. There are currently no known workarounds.
descriptions.label: default

descriptions.data:
Applications commonly use cryptography to implement authentication mechanisms and to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive data, both in transit and at rest.  The proper and accurate implementation of cryptography is extremely critical to its efficacy.  Configuration or coding mistakes as well as incorrect assumptions may negate a large degree of the protection it affords, leaving the crypto implementation vulnerable to attack.
Common cryptographic mistakes include, but are not limited to, selecting weak keys or weak cipher modes, unintentionally exposing sensitive cryptographic data, using predictable entropy sources, and mismanaging or hard-coding keys.  
Developers often make the dangerous assumption that they can improve security by designing their own cryptographic algorithm; however, one of the basic tenets of cryptography is that any cipher whose effectiveness is reliant on the secrecy of the algorithm is fundamentally flawed.
descriptions.label: default

tags.cweDescription: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute Description: Setting the Secure attribute on an HTTP cookie instructs the web browser to send it only over a secure channel, such as a TLS connection.  Issuing a cookie without the Secure attribute allows the browser to transmit it over unencrypted connections, which are susceptible to eavesdropping.  It is particularly important to set the Secure attribute on any cookies containing sensitive data, such as authentication information (e.g. "remember me" style functionality).;

input.title: no title on the later member

cases.name: first-wins keeps the first member absence over a later member value
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: ADR-0017 §6 says first-wins, not first-non-empty: an absent field on the first member stays absent.

input.title: only the later member has a title

cases.name: controlType, verificationMethod and applicability first-win
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: Requirement-level classification, not per instance.

cases.name: cvss, epss and kev first-win
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: These describe the vulnerability, not the instance, so the later members add nothing.

cases.name: impact, severity and effectiveImpact are worst-wins
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: Worst-wins regardless of member order: the later, worse member wins.

cases.name: worst-wins is not last-wins
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: The same pair in the other order gives the same answer.

cases.name: cwe, refs, externalReferences, evidence, statusOverrides and poams union
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: Each list keeps its first-seen order and drops the repeated member: cwe by the string, the rest by the whole value, which is the only key that cannot discard a distinct member.

cases.name: tags union per array-valued key, first-win per scalar key, and a later-only key is added
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: nist unions and de-duplicates AC-1; the scalar severity first-wins; cci exists only on the later member and is added, because the rule is stated per key.

cases.name: a tag key whose members disagree on shape first-wins
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: Only a key both members carry as an array unions; anything else falls to first-wins.

cases.name: effectiveStatus, disposition and effectiveChecksum are dropped, not merged
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: ADR-0017 §6 derives these after merging from the merged results and overrides; the first member values describe only that member, so carrying them would be wrong data.

cases.name: affectedPackages de-duplicate on purl
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: Same purl on both members: one entry survives.

cases.name: affectedPackages without a purl de-duplicate on name and version
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: ADR-0017 §6 names name + version, not ecosystem: the differing ecosystem does not make a second entry.

cases.name: identical results are both kept — results are never de-duplicated
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: A divergence from heimdall2's collapseResults flag (base-converter.ts:167): ADR-0017 §6 says concatenate, full stop. Each result is one source finding, and dropping one would lose a finding the result-count anchor is there to catch.

cases.name: a slice with no repeated id is returned unchanged
cases.source: constructed
cases.note: Same length, same order, same values.

cases.name: the survivor sits at the position of its first member
cases.source: constructed
cases.note: V-2 is emitted first at index 1 and stays at index 1 even though its second member trails V-3.

cases.name: entries with an empty id pass through untouched and never merge
cases.source: constructed — mirrors the adversarial corpus requirement-missing-id case
cases.note: Divergence from heimdall2, which drops an item whose key is not a string outright (base-converter.ts:120-123, no else). id is schema-required, so an empty one is malformed input: HDF keeps it and keeps the document diffable rather than silently shrinking it.

cases.name: an empty slice rolls up to an empty slice
cases.source: constructed
cases.note: A baseline with no requirements is not an error.

cases.name: the unrated-severity marker survives when every member is unrated
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: severity_rating is DERIVED, not a scalar tag: it survives only as an AND across the members. Both members unrated, so the merged requirement is still unrated. This is the shape grype's real Grype/CVE-2024-2511 group has today — marker on both, severity absent, impact 0.5.

cases.name: the unrated-severity marker is dropped when a later member was rated
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: The self-contradiction case a plain scalar-tag merge would produce: firstWins would keep the marker while worst-wins takes the later member's genuine high, yielding severity high alongside severity_rating unrated. The marker is dropped instead.

cases.name: the unrated-severity marker is not added from a later member alone
cases.source: constructed — no committed golden exercises this rule
cases.note: The mirror case: under the ratified later-only-key rule a plain scalar tag WOULD be added, labelling a requirement unrated although the first member carried a genuine rating. Being derived, it is not added.
